meanings.usage: 指远古生物的遗骸、遗迹经地质作用形成的石头，也可引申指思想守旧的人
指民间口头流传的历史相关故事，也可指传奇人物
强调使事物保持原有状态不被损坏，也可指食物保鲜、腌制
指详细复述已经发生的事，宾语多为故事、经历等
指讲述家族、民族历史的长篇传奇叙事
可指人类、动物的大规模迁居，也可指数据、人口的流动迁移
指研究人类起源、发展、文化习俗的专业学者
可表示时间、空间上的遥远，也可指关系疏远

meanings.meaning: 祖先，祖宗（指家族或民族的先辈，反义词为descendant（后代））

meanings.usage: 指通过研究古代遗存、文物还原历史的专业学者
指一种坚硬的硅质岩石，古时用于制作工具或取火
指将材料加工为特定形状，也可引申为影响、塑造性格、观点等
指有机体被微生物分解变质，也可引申为制度、社会衰败
强调逐渐分解变坏的过程，可用于物质、建筑、社会制度等

phrases.usage: 动词短语，指将传统、故事、财产等代代传承，常用被动语态be handed down

examples.en: These traditional crafts are handed down from generation to generation in this village.
examples.zh: 这些传统手工艺在这个村子里代代相传。

phrases.usage: 固定搭配，指读到、获悉某类信息，相当于read about

examples.en: I read of his outstanding contributions to medical research in the newspaper.
examples.zh: 我在报纸上读到了他在医学研究方面做出的杰出贡献。

phrases.usage: 副词短语，在句中作状语，表示一代接一代地

examples.en: The custom of eating mooncakes on Mid-Autumn Festival has been kept from generation to generation.
examples.zh: 中秋节吃月饼的习俗被一代又一代地保留了下来。

phrases.usage: 并列连词短语，连接两个并列成分，表示“既不…也不…”，连接主语时谓语动词遵循就近原则

examples.en: Neither my parents nor I am interested in this reality show.
examples.zh: 我父母和我对这个真人秀都不感兴趣。

phrases.usage: 动词短语，指完全腐烂、烂掉，强调腐烂的最终结果

examples.en: The fallen leaves on the ground will rot away and become nutrients for the soil.
examples.zh: 地上的落叶会腐烂掉，变成土壤的养分。

phrases.usage: 副词短语，在句中作状语，表示毫无踪迹、无影无踪

examples.en: The plane crashed into the mountain and disappeared without trace.
examples.zh: 飞机撞上山后就消失得无影无踪了。

phrases.usage: 副词短语，表强调，意为“即使到现在，即便在如今”

examples.en: Even now, many people in remote mountain areas still have no access to the Internet.
examples.zh: 即使到现在，很多偏远山区的人们依然无法使用互联网。

phrases.usage: 副词短语，指很久以前，常用于一般过去时的句子中

examples.en: Long ago, there lived a kind old man in this small town.
examples.zh: 很久以前，这个小镇上住着一位善良的老人。

grammar.title: 关系副词where与关系代词who引导的限定性定语从句
grammar.structure: 1. 表地点的先行词 + where + 完整从句；2. 表人的先行词 + who + 从句（who充当主语/宾语）
grammar.definition: 限定性定语从句用于修饰先行词，对先行词的范围进行限定，删除从句后主句意思会不完整。where指代表示地点的先行词，在从句中作地点状语；who指代表示人的先行词，在从句中作主语或宾语。 当需要对表示地点、人的名词进行限定说明时使用，使表达更准确具体。

examples.en: We can read of things that happened 5, 000 years ago in the Near East, where people first learned to write.
examples.zh: 我们可以了解到5000年前近东发生的事情，那里的人最早学会了写字。

examples.en: The professor who gave us a speech last week will come to our school again tomorrow.
examples.zh: 上周给我们做演讲的那位教授明天会再次来我们学校。

grammar.title: may have done结构表对过去的推测
grammar.structure: 主语 + may/might + have + 动词过去分词
grammar.definition: 该结构用于表示说话人对过去已经发生的事情的不确定推测，推测发生的可能性中等，语气较为委婉。 当没有确切证据证明过去某事是否发生，仅进行可能性推测时使用。

examples.en: They may also have used wood and skins, but these have rotted away.
examples.zh: 他们也可能使用过木头和兽皮，但这些东西都已经腐烂了。

examples.en: She may have forgotten to inform us of the change of the meeting time.
examples.zh: 她可能忘记通知我们会议时间变更的事了。

patterns.pattern: The only way that sb can do sth is to do sth

original.en: The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas legends handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.
original.zh: 他们保存历史的唯一方法是将历史当作由一代又一代讲述人传承的英雄传说来复述。

imitations.en: The only way that you can get high marks in the final exam is to review all the lessons carefully.
imitations.zh: 你在期末考试中取得高分的唯一方法是认真复习所有课程。

imitations.en: The only way that the company can reduce costs is to improve production efficiency.
imitations.zh: 这家公司降低成本的唯一方法是提升生产效率。

patterns.pattern: These ... are useful because they can tell us something about ...

original.en: These legends are useful because they can tell us something about migrations of people who lived long ago.
original.zh: 这些传说很有用，因为它们能告诉我们生活在很久以前的人类迁徙的相关信息。

imitations.en: These old photos are useful because they can tell us something about the city's great changes in the past 30 years.
imitations.zh: 这些老照片很有用，因为它们能告诉我们这座城市过去30年的巨大变化的相关信息。

imitations.en: These survey data are useful because they can tell us something about consumers' preference for new energy vehicles.
imitations.zh: 这些调查数据很有用，因为它们能告诉我们消费者对新能源汽车的偏好的相关信息。

patterns.pattern: ..., and so ... have remained when even ... have disappeared.

original.en: Stone does not decay, and so the tools of long ago have remained when even the bones of the men who made them have disappeared without trace.
original.zh: 石头不会腐烂，因此即使制造这些工具的人的骨头已经消失得无影无踪，远古的工具依然保留了下来。

imitations.en: Paper is easy to preserve, and so the ancient books written thousands of years ago have remained when even the palaces where they were stored have disappeared.
imitations.zh: 纸张容易保存，因此即使存放这些古籍的宫殿已经消失，数千年前写下的古籍依然留存了下来。

imitations.en: True love does not change, and so the promise they made to each other has remained when even the ring that witnessed their engagement has been lost.
imitations.zh: 真爱不会改变，因此即使见证他们订婚的戒指已经丢失，他们对彼此许下的承诺依然留存。

text.title: First listen and then answer the following question.

lines.en: We can read of things that happened 5,000 years ago in the Near East, where people first learned to write.
lines.zh: 我们从书籍中可读到5,000年前近东发生的事情，那里的人最早学会了写字。

lines.en: But there are some parts of the world where even now people cannot write.
lines.zh: 但直到现在,世界上有些地方，人们还不会书写。

lines.en: The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas -- legends handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.
lines.zh: 他们保存历史的唯一办法是将历史当作传说讲述，由讲述人一代接一代地将史实描述为传奇故事口传下来。

lines.en: These legends are useful because they can tell us something about migrations of people who lived long ago, but none could write down what they did. Anthropologists wondered where the remote ancestors of the Polynesian peoples now living in the Pacific Islands came from.
lines.zh: 人类学家过去不清楚如今生活在太平洋诸岛上的波利尼西亚人的祖先来自何方，当地人的传说却告诉人们：其中一部分是约在2,000年前从印度尼西亚迁来的。

lines.en: The sagas of these people explain that some of them came from Indonesia about 2,000 years ago.
lines.zh: 但是，和我们相似的原始人生活的年代太久远了，因此，有关他们的传说既使有如今也失传了。

lines.en: But the first people who were like ourselves lived so long ago that even their sagas, if they had any, are forgotten.
lines.zh: 于是，考古学家们既缺乏历史记载，又无口头传说来帮助他们弄清最早的“现代人”是从哪里来的。

lines.en: So archaeologists have neither history nor legends to help them to find out where the first 'modern men' came from.
lines.zh: 然而，幸运的是，远古人用石头制作了工具，特别是用燧石，因为燧石较之其他石头更容易成形。

lines.en: Fortunately, however, ancient men made tools of stone, especially flint, because this is easier to shape than other kinds.
lines.zh: 他们也可能用过木头和兽皮，但这类东西早已腐烂殆尽。

lines.en: They may also have used wood and skins, but these have rotted away.
Stone does not decay, and so the tools of long ago have remained when even the bones of the men who made them have disappeared without trace.
lines.zh: 因此，尽管制造这些工具的人的骨头早已荡然无存，但远古时代的石头工具却保存了下来。

questions.q: Why are legends handed down by storytellers useful?
questions.zh: 为什么由讲述人代代相传的传说是有用的？
questions.a: Because they can tell us something about migrations of people who lived long ago, but none could write down what they did.
questions.aZh: 因为它们能告诉我们一些关于很久以前生活、却无人能记录下自己所作所为的人群迁徙的情况。
questions.hint: 见课文第三句 These legends are useful because...

questions.q: What is the only way for people in some parts of the world to preserve their history?
questions.zh: 世界上某些地方的人保存自己历史的唯一办法是什么？
questions.a: To recount it as sagas -- legends handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.
questions.aZh: 把历史当作传奇故事讲述，即由讲述人一代代传下来的传说。
questions.hint: 见课文第二、三句 The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas.

questions.q: What did the sagas of the Polynesian peoples explain about their ancestors?
questions.zh: 波利尼西亚人的传说对他们的祖先作了什么说明？
questions.a: They explain that some of them came from Indonesia about 2,000 years ago.
questions.aZh: 传说说明他们中的一部分人是约两千年前从印度尼西亚迁来的。
questions.hint: 见课文第五句 The sagas of these people explain...

questions.q: Why have the tools of long ago remained while the bones of the men who made them disappeared?
questions.zh: 为什么远古时代的工具能保存下来，而制造它们的人的骨头却消失了？
questions.a: Because stone does not decay, so the tools of long ago have remained when even the bones of the men who made them have disappeared without trace.
questions.aZh: 因为石头不会腐烂，所以远古时代的工具得以留存，而制造它们的人的骨头却荡然无存。
questions.hint: 见课文最后一句 Stone does not decay...

questions.q: Why do you think archaeologists can only rely on stone tools, rather than on legends, to study the first 'modern men'?
questions.zh: 你认为考古学家为什么只能依靠石器，而不能依靠传说来研究最早的“现代人”？
questions.a: Because the first people like ourselves lived so long ago that even their sagas, if they had any, are forgotten; only stone, which does not decay, survives.
questions.aZh: 因为和我们相似的远古人类生活年代太久远，即便有过传说也已失传，只有不会腐烂的石头才留存下来。
questions.hint: 综合课文第五至八句推断

translation:
我们从书籍中可读到5,000年前近东发生的事情，那里的人最早学会了写字。
但直到现在,世界上有些地方，人们还不会书写。
他们保存历史的唯一办法是将历史当作传说讲述，由讲述人一代接一代地将史实描述为传奇故事口传下来。
人类学家过去不清楚如今生活在太平洋诸岛上的波利尼西亚人的祖先来自何方，当地人的传说却告诉人们：其中一部分是约在2,000年前从印度尼西亚迁来的。
但是，和我们相似的原始人生活的年代太久远了，因此，有关他们的传说既使有如今也失传了。
于是，考古学家们既缺乏历史记载，又无口头传说来帮助他们弄清最早的“现代人”是从哪里来的。
然而，幸运的是，远古人用石头制作了工具，特别是用燧石，因为燧石较之其他石头更容易成形。
他们也可能用过木头和兽皮，但这类东西早已腐烂殆尽。
石头是不会腐烂的。
因此，尽管制造这些工具的人的骨头早已荡然无存，但远古时代的石头工具却保存了下来。

title: Finding Fossil Man
subtitle: 寻找化石人

lead.question: 为什么由讲述人代代相传、保存历史的传说对研究远古人类仍然有用？
lead.warmup: 在文字出现之前，人类靠口耳相传的传奇故事保存历史。本文从近东最早的文字讲起，引出至今仍不会书写的民族：他们只能把往事编成 saga，一代代讲述。传说帮人类学家追问波利尼西亚人祖先的来处。当传说也随年代久远而失传，考古学家只能转向不会腐烂的石器，寻找最早的“现代人”从何而来。
goals: 掌握 fossil、remains、archaeologist、primitive、flint 等本课核心词的用法
理解 sagas、legends 作为口传历史的作用，抓住听力提问的答案线索
复习被动语态、现在完成时与定语从句在文中的实际运用
能用英语复述人类学家与考古学家探索早期现代人起源的思路
lead.summary: 课文先指出近东最早出现文字，而世界某些地方至今没有文字，只能把历史编成 saga 由讲述人代代传下。传说能帮人类学家追溯远古人群的迁徙，如波利尼西亚人的部分祖先约两千年前来自印度尼西亚。但更早的“现代人”连传说都已失传，考古学家只好依靠不会腐烂的石器，凭石制工具推断他们的踪迹。
lead.tips: 易错提醒：remain 常作不及物动词，意为“剩下、留下”，remains 才表示“遗迹、遗骸”；decay 指自然腐坏，与 preserve（保存、留存）语义相反。

exercises.q: 汉译英：这些化石遗骸能告诉我们远古人类的迁徙情况。
exercises.a: These fossil remains can tell us something about the migrations of ancient men.

exercises.q: 汉译英：他们保存历史的唯一办法就是把历史当作传奇故事讲述。
exercises.a: The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas.

exercises.q: 填空：____ have neither history nor legends to help them find out where the first 'modern men' came from.
填空：Stone does not ____, and so the tools of ____ men have remained.
句型转换（定语从句）：合并 We can read of things. They happened 5,000 years ago in the Near East.
exercises.a: We can read of things that happened 5,000 years ago in the Near East.

exercises.q: 句型转换（现在完成时被动）：Legends are handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.
exercises.a: Legends have been handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.

exercises.q: 改错：The sagas of these people explain that some of them have come from the island of Java about 2,000 years ago.
exercises.a: The sagas of these people explain that some of them came from the island of Java about 2,000 years ago.
exercises.note: 有明确过去时间用一般过去时

quiz.q: 根据课文，人们最早学会写字是在哪里？
世界上有些地方的人保存自己历史的唯一办法是什么？
options: To write it down in books

quiz.q: 波利尼西亚人的传说说明他们的一部分祖先来自哪里？
考古学家为什么难以弄清最早的“现代人”来自哪里？
options: They have no stone tools to study
They live far from the Pacific
They have neither history nor legends to help them

quiz.q: 为什么远古石制工具能留存，而制造者的骨头却消失了？
options: Because flint is soft and light

quiz.q: 根据课文，远古人为什么特别选用燧石制作工具？
options: Because it was handed down as a saga
Because it is easier to shape than other kinds
Because it is easier to find than wood
